To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the energy encircled within a circular detector of finite diameter by a zoneplate is the convolution of the energy distribution of the source with a wavenumberspread function, that the wavenumber spread is invariant for a given ratio of the sensor radius to the Airy radius, and that for a given sensor radius the energy encirclement is maximum for a Lorentz source of halfwidth equal to the sensor diameter.

a circular zoneplate lens with a circular sensor at the focal plane can be used as a scanning spectrometer or monochromator, and that the energy intercepted by a sensor of a given size is a function of wavelenght, the distance between the sensor and the focal plane, the number of zones of the zoneplate, and the size of the sensor relative to the size of the Airy disc.

the spectral resolution of a zone-plate lens with circular sensor is a function of the product of the distance to the focal plane and the number of zones in the zoneplate, and that the spectral resolution is independent of the ratio of the sensor radius to Airly radius.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spectral resolution of a zone-plate lens with a circular sensor.
a zoneplate lens and a circular detector, which are combined in a zoneplate lens-sensor combination.
the use of a zoneplate lens in combination with a circular sensor to obtain a high-resolution spectrum of a source.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the zoneplate lens with circular aperture is a very efficient optical element for use in conjunction with a circular sensor.
, in the absence of a more rigorous theory, it appears that the zoneplate lens is not a suitable optical element for the design of a spectrometer or a monochromator.

a zoneplate lens with a small circular sensor can be used to measure the spectral distribution of the source with a resolution that is a function of the number of zone pairs and the ratio of the radius of the sensor to the Airy radius of the zoneplate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spectral resolution is determined by the number of zones in the zoneplate, and the angular resolution is determined by sensor radius and the number of zones.
a sensor-zoneplate combination has a spectral resolving power that is a function of the product of the sensor radius and the zoneplate focal ratio.
the sensor-zone- plate lens combination is an efficient and convenient means of spectral resolution of a point source.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the wavenumber spread of the energy intercepted is a function only of the product of the sensor radius and the number of zones of the zoneplate lens.
the spectral resolution of a zone plate with a small sensor is not limited by the number of zones.
the spectral resolution of the zoneplate is not a function of the number of rings in the zoneplate.
